verdict_text:
YES

The merge logic matches the specification: it maps `base_model.model.` + `gpt_neox.layers.<i>.attention.query_key_value` adapter names to the base names, reads `scale = lora_alpha / r = 2` and `fan_in_fan_out` from the config rather than hardcoding them, computes `B @ A` (float32, no transposition since `fan_in_fan_out` is false), adds it to the float32-upcast base weight and casts back to the original float16 dtype in place under the same key. No adapter or intermediate tensor enters `sd`, and all other base tensors are untouched. All four required checks (16 pairs merged, no `lora_` name, `[6144, 2048]` shape, 244 tensors) are asserted before the write.

One thing I could not verify from what was provided: clause 4's sharding behaviour lives entirely in `_ckpt.save_sharded_safetensors`, whose source is not part of the artifact shown here; the call site passes the correct 536,870,912-byte limit and output directory.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm). verdict none = no answer, excluded from rates.
